headline: Apple takes OpenAI to court over stolen secrets

sources.title: Apple sues OpenAI alleging trade secret theft
Apple accuses OpenAI of using stolen trade secrets in new lawsuit
Apple sues OpenAI, alleging the AI company stole trade secrets
Apple sues OpenAI and two former employees over alleged trade secret theft (video, NBC News)

chunks.text: Two of the [[biggest names]] in technology have {{fallen out}}. Apple, [[the company behind]] the iPhone, has filed a [[lawsuit]] against OpenAI, [[the maker of]] ChatGPT. A few of Apple's workers left the company to join OpenAI, and Apple [[claims]] that when they went, they {{walked off with}} [[confidential]] information that helped OpenAI {{come up with}} a new AI [[device]].

verbs.wrong: To become less successful than a rival
verbs.correct: To stop being partners after a quarrel
verbs.why: Old friends can fall out over money, and business partners can fall out after a serious disagreement. Apple and OpenAI have now fallen out too, with Apple accusing its former partner of stealing company secrets.

verbs.wrong: To leave a job suddenly, without warning
verbs.correct: To take something that does not belong to you
verbs.why: A careless guest can walk off with a hotel towel, and a quick thief can walk off with an unlocked bike. Apple claims that departing workers walked off with confidential files on their way out the door.

verbs.wrong: To improve a product that already exists
verbs.correct: To think of or create a new idea or plan
verbs.why: Engineers come up with a clever fix under a tight deadline, and writers come up with a fresh idea after months of trying. Apple claims OpenAI could never have come up with its new device without those stolen files.

chunks.text: In its [[court papers]], Apple {{lays out}} how it believes the [[theft]] happened. It says that before these workers left, they {{sent off}} [[private]] company files to their own personal email accounts. Apple now wants a [[judge]] to {{step in}} and stop OpenAI from using any of its [[trade secrets]].

verbs.wrong: To prove that something really happened
verbs.correct: To explain or describe something clearly
verbs.why: A coach lays out the game plan before kickoff, and a lawyer lays out the evidence piece by piece. Apple's court papers lay out exactly how it believes the theft of its secrets happened.

verbs.wrong: To hide something so that nobody can find it
verbs.correct: To send something to a place, often by email or mail
verbs.why: Families send off holiday cards every December, and a busy office sends off bills at the end of each month. Apple says the workers sent off private company files to their own personal email accounts before they quit.

verbs.wrong: To write a long report about a past event
verbs.correct: To get involved in order to help or stop a problem
verbs.why: A manager steps in when two coworkers cannot agree, and a government sometimes steps in to save a struggling bank. Apple now wants a judge to step in and stop OpenAI from using its trade secrets.

chunks.text: OpenAI quickly {{hit back}} at the claims. A [[spokesperson]] for the company said that OpenAI has [[no interest in]] other companies' secrets, and that its [[lawyers]] are still {{going over}} the papers. [[So far]], [[the two sides]] do not agree, and neither one will {{back down}}.

verbs.wrong: To refuse to answer questions about a problem
verbs.correct: To reply strongly to an attack or criticism
verbs.why: A mayor hits back at unfair criticism in a press conference, and a company hits back at a bad review with its own statement. OpenAI quickly hit back at Apple's claims, saying it has no interest in stealing anyone's secrets.

verbs.wrong: To correct the mistakes in a document
verbs.correct: To examine or check something carefully
verbs.why: A student goes over class notes the night before a test, and a lawyer goes over a contract twice before signing. OpenAI's lawyers are now going over Apple's court papers before they decide what to say next.

verbs.wrong: To admit that you did something wrong
verbs.correct: To stop demanding something or stop arguing
verbs.why: A union refuses to back down during a pay dispute, and a politician sometimes backs down first when the facts turn against him. So far, neither Apple nor OpenAI will back down in this fight.

chunks.text: The fight comes as Apple {{moves away}} from OpenAI in another way. Apple has announced that its [[voice assistant]], Siri, will soon {{run on}} Google's Gemini system [[instead of]] ChatGPT. Many people had expected the two companies to {{stick together}} [[for years to come]], so the sudden change has surprised the whole tech world.

verbs.why: A bakery can move away from plastic packaging over a few years, and a company can slowly move away from an old business partner. Apple is now moving away from ChatGPT, giving its voice assistant Siri to Google's Gemini system instead.

verbs.wrong: To be owned by another company
verbs.correct: To work using a certain kind of power
verbs.why: An old car runs on gas, and a whole factory can run on solar power alone. Soon Apple's Siri will run on Google's Gemini system instead of the ChatGPT technology it used before.

verbs.wrong: To share their technology with each other
verbs.correct: To stay united and continue to support each other
verbs.why: Neighbors stick together during a bad storm, and teammates stick together even after a painful loss. Many people had expected Apple and OpenAI to stick together for years, so this sudden split surprised the whole tech world.

mainIdea.s: Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, saying former workers walked off with secret files. Apple wants a judge to step in and stop OpenAI from using this information.
mainIdea.why: Apple filed a lawsuit claiming workers who left for OpenAI took confidential files. It wants a judge to step in and stop OpenAI from using its trade secrets.

mainIdea.s: OpenAI admitted that it used stolen files from Apple to build its brand new voice device. The company said it would pay Apple and stop selling any products right away.
mainIdea.why: Close, but OpenAI did not admit any theft. It hit back at the claims and said it has no interest in other companies' secrets.

mainIdea.s: Last year, Apple and Google settled a separate dispute over how phones share user data with advertisers. Both companies agreed to change their privacy rules within months.
mainIdea.why: This story is about the new Apple lawsuit against OpenAI over trade secrets, not an older Apple and Google privacy dispute.

lines.text: Big tech drama. Apple and OpenAI have completely {{fallen out}}.
They were. But some Apple workers left to join OpenAI, and Apple says they {{walked off with}} confidential files that helped OpenAI {{come up with}} a new AI device.
[[That's a big accusation]]. Can Apple prove it?
In its court papers, Apple {{lays out}} the whole story. It claims the workers {{sent off}} private files to their personal email accounts before leaving.
And what does Apple want now?
A judge to {{step in}} and stop OpenAI from using any trade secrets.
They {{hit back}} right away. Their lawyers are still {{going over}} the papers, but the company says it has no interest in anyone's secrets. Neither side will {{back down}}.
[[Ouch]]. And didn't Apple also pick Google for Siri?
Yes, Apple is {{moving away}} from OpenAI there too. Siri will soon {{run on}} Google's Gemini instead of ChatGPT.
Everyone expected them to {{stick together}}. [[So much for that]].

expressions.def: Used when someone is blamed for something very serious
ex: You think he lied? That's a big accusation.

expressions.def: Used to react to something painful or embarrassing
ex: They canceled his show after one episode. Ouch.

expressions.def: Used when a plan or idea has clearly failed
ex: It's raining. So much for our picnic.
